card: Bitcoin Core previously trusted external signers completely when signing transactions, replacing the wallet's PSBT wholesale with whatever the signer returned. This PR hardens external signer processing by merging the response into the original PSBT, verifying matching PSBT versions, rejecting finalized inputs, and rejecting signatures with unsafe sighash types like SIGHASH_NONE or SIGHASH_SINGLE. It also revamps the functional test mock signer into a dynamic offline descriptor wallet to test tampered and misbehaving signers, and enforces IWYU for the external signer module.
changed_since_previous: Added IWYU enforcement for src/external_signer.cpp in CI and cleaned up headers.
evidence: Commit 2b801fc384: 'Previously the PSBT returned by the external signer replaced the original wholesale, trusting the signer not to modify the transaction. Merge it instead. This rejects a response that describes a different transaction.'

Commit 4110fbd057: 'A signature with SIGHASH_NONE or SIGHASH_SINGLE doesn't commit to all outputs, letting anyone alter them after signing. Reject a PSBT from an external signer that declares such a sighash type or contains signatures made with one.'
Description: 'This PR absorbs the scenarios from #35358, but is better able to test them thanks to the new mock signer implementation.'
problem: Bitcoin Core previously replaced its PSBT wholesale with whatever an external signer returned, trusting hardware devices or intermediate bridge software not to tamper with outputs, sequence numbers, or sighash flags. A compromised or buggy signer could finalize inputs, divert funds to fees, alter outputs, or use unsafe sighash types that allow third parties to modify outputs. Furthermore, the functional test framework's mock signer was static and could only replay hardcoded PSBTs, preventing automated testing of malicious signer behavior.

risk.why: A flaw in sighash inspection or PSBT merging could cause valid hardware wallet responses to be rejected, breaking external signer transactions for users.

scope_notes: Most of the diff is in Python functional test harnesses (327 lines added across mock and functional tests); C++ changes in src/external_signer.cpp are about 60 lines.
summary: Hardens external signer PSBT handling in the wallet by merging the returned PSBT into the original instead of replacing it, enforcing matching PSBT versions, rejecting finalized inputs, and rejecting signatures that use unsafe sighash types (SIGHASH_NONE or SIGHASH_SINGLE). It also revamps the functional test external signer mock to use an offline descriptor wallet capable of simulating misbehaving or stripped signer responses, and enforces include-what-you-use (IWYU) on external signer code.
